body:
zmx's control surface is one unix socket per session under a per-UID runtime dir, and ssh can forward a unix socket to a unix socket. If that works, a remote session is an `ssh -N -L` away and zmux needs no transport at all — the same labels and list apply across machines, with the machine name as one more field.

Unverified, and worth checking before any design that mentions remote: whether zmx tolerates the latency and the peer credentials of a forwarded socket, and whether forwarded socket paths can collide with local ones (both live in the same per-UID dir, so names would need a machine prefix). Not v0.
title: Remote sessions need no server, only a forwarded socket
